headline: Chips Ignite a Lopsided Midday Rally as Optical Names Surge
body_html:
Stocks are climbing at midday Monday, and the advance is lopsided. Of the 524 names in our universe, 447 are higher and only 74 lower. Prices are still moving and are not final, but the tone is plainly constructive.

Semiconductors set the pace, up 5.29% on average, well clear of industrials at 2.77%, materials at 2.38% and homebuilders at 2.05%. Consumer, software, energy and healthcare are all higher too, with healthcare the softest of the group at 1.00%. The standouts sit in the networking and hardware complex: Bloom Energy is up 12.08%, Coherent 11.63%, Flex 10.82% and Ciena 10.44%. Hims & Hers Health, down 6.31%, and LegalZoom, down 5.54%, lead the decliners.

Easing oil prices are helping the backdrop, and Asian stocks held steady as worries over AI and the Middle East receded. Into the close, watch whether chip leadership holds after such a sharp move, and whether Iran diplomacy, including the planned White House meeting with Qatar's prime minister, upsets the calm ahead of Tuesday's session.

briefs.headline: Optical and networking names lead the charge
briefs.body: Coherent and Ciena are each up more than 10% at midday, and contract manufacturer Flex is close behind. The gains suggest buyers are chasing the hardware behind data-center networking. Moves this large this early can fade, so the close will show how much conviction is behind them.

briefs.headline: Pockets of weakness: telehealth, legal services, biotech
briefs.body: Hims & Hers Health is down 6.31% and LegalZoom 5.54%, the steepest declines in our universe. Biotechs TG Therapeutics and Sarepta are also lower, along with solar maker First Solar and chocolate maker Hershey. With so few stocks falling, these stand out as isolated stock-specific moves.

briefs.headline: Trump to meet Qatar's leader as Iran talks stall
briefs.body: The president is due to meet Qatar's prime minister, whose country is mediating, but no deal to end the war looks close. Iran is defending its two-day proposal for peace talks after Washington rejected its conditions. Markets are treating the diplomacy as slow-moving for now.

briefs.headline: Hormuz traffic quiet after navigation aids destroyed
briefs.body: Iran says no unauthorised vessels passed through the Strait of Hormuz overnight, after navigation aids there were destroyed. Separately, Saudi Arabia said the danger had passed in Riyadh following an alert, a day after a Houthi attack. Regional risk remains a live variable for energy traders.

briefs.headline: Gold firms as cheaper oil eases inflation worries
briefs.body: Gold is higher as falling oil prices take some pressure off inflation fears. Indian shares closed at an eight-month high on the same drop in crude, and Asian stocks were steady. A firm dollar, tied to bets on the Fed, is the counterweight.

briefs.headline: Lilly's obesity pill shows promise in sleep apnea
briefs.body: Eli Lilly reported that its oral obesity treatment eased sleep apnea in a late-stage trial, a result that could open the way to regulatory approval for that use. Healthcare is up 1.00% at midday, the smallest sector gain, so the news is not yet driving the group.
